title: ack
description: Daemon -> client handshake response. accepted=false carries an error and ends the session. This is the ONLY place a client learns what robot it is talking to: see `descriptor` (what it can move) and `capabilities` (what verbs it honours). Clients MUST derive behaviour from those, never from `model`.

model.description: ADVISORY ONLY. The robot's model/generation label (e.g. "L2", "L3"). Provided so logs, dataset provenance and bug reports can name the hardware. Clients MUST NOT branch behaviour on this value -- branch on `descriptor` and `capabilities` instead, so a new model works against an unmodified client. Deliberately not an enum: enumerating models here would mean a schema edit per model, which is exactly the coupling this field exists to avoid. Absent on robots predating the field.

capabilities.description: Optional verbs this robot honours, beyond the always-present core (control jog, control action, command, telemetry). A client MUST treat an absent capability as unsupported, and MUST ignore an unrecognised entry rather than failing. This exists because capability differences are NOT expressible as DOFs: a descriptor cannot say whether absolute lift targets are accepted or whether two-way audio exists. Known values: "task_jog" (cylindrical/task-space arm jog), "leader_action_deg" (absolute leader-arm degrees), "lift_targets" (absolute <side>_lift.pos height targets in mm), "record" (dataset recording verbs), "policy_stream", "call" (two-way audio), "perception", "pose_targets" (absolute Cartesian pose targets via control.pose), "named_navigation" (map-bound named waypoints through session navigation frames), and "sensor_streams" (opt-in LiDAR/IMU session frames). Absent field means UNKNOWN, not none -- robots predating the field must be probed or assumed legacy. WHO FILLS THIS: it is a UNION built along the path. A daemon lists what it itself honours (task_jog, leader_action_deg, lift_targets); a bridge APPENDS what it adds on top (record, policy_stream, call, named_navigation, sensor_streams) before forwarding, because the daemon cannot know which services a bridge in front of it exposes. On a merged stack like the L3 gateway one process fills the whole list. A client therefore sees one flat list and must not infer which component provides a given capability.

norm_mode.description: Normalization mode of all .pos values in state/action.

descriptor.description: What this robot physically is. OPTIONAL, and its ABSENCE is meaningful: a robot that sends no descriptor is a legacy unit whose DOF vocabulary the client must already know (the L2 daemon is one -- see MODELS.md). Present-and-populated is the only case in which a client may drive DOFs it did not know about in advance.

joints.description: Every drivable "<motor>.pos" key. This is the authoritative joint vocabulary; a client must build its keymap from this rather than from a compiled-in list.

base.description: Base DOFs in the TELEMETRY namespace ("x.vel", "theta.vel"). WARNING: this is NOT the jog namespace. A control jog addresses the base as {"base":{"linear":r,"angular":r}} -- see control.json. The two vocabularies are different on purpose (telemetry reports measured axis velocities; jog expresses normalized drive intent) and confusing them yields a frame the robot parses as a full stop.

aux.description: Non-arm actuators addressable by jog, e.g. "left_lift"/"right_lift". A robot with lifts MUST list them here; leaving this empty while accepting lift jog makes the lifts undiscoverable and is a defect.

cameras.description: Camera roles, for logging and diagnostics ONLY. This does NOT drive video: the robot sends one composited H.264 track and describes its tiling in camera_layout.json, which is authoritative and independent of this field. Do not derive a layout from this list.

ranges.description: Authoritative [min, max] per "<name>.pos". Values outside are CLAMPED robot-side, never rejected, so use these to scale input rather than to pre-validate. A joint absent from this map has no advertised range and a client must not invent one.

jog_scale.description:
How a normalized jog rate converts to real motion on THIS robot. Optional; absent means the robot does not advertise it and a client MUST NOT assume a value -- the L2 fleet is frozen and will never send this, so absent is the common case for years.

WHAT IT PROMISES: the NOMINAL COMMANDED scale, i.e. multiply your normalized rate in [-1,1] by this to get the rate the robot will command under nominal conditions. It is NOT a guarantee of achieved velocity, and three things routinely make the achieved rate lower: the watchdog's warn state scales all motion to ZERO until control frames resume (watch telemetry.status.watchdog); an acceleration limit means short jogs never reach the rate at all; and on stacks running MoveIt Servo, singularity and collision scaling reduce it near limits. A client that needs the achieved rate must measure it from telemetry -- which is precisely what these units are chosen to allow.

UNITS ARE PER NAMESPACE, and each is the unit of the thing it addresses, so that a client can close the loop against telemetry and verify what it got:
  joints  normalized units per second, matching telemetry `state` and descriptor `ranges` (norm_mode units, so [-100,100] under range_m100_100). Deliberately NOT rad/s: telemetry reports normalized positions, so a rate in rad/s could not be checked against anything the client can see. Expect these to DIFFER per joint even when the robot uses one internal rad/s constant, because the normalized-to-physical scale is per joint.
  lift    millimetres per second, matching the mm of `<side>_lift.pos` absolute targets.
  task    SI -- metres/second for x, y and z, radians/second for pitch and yaw (and its deprecated alias shoulder_pan). These are Cartesian VERBS with no position key to match, so SI is the only sensible choice.
  base    metres/second and radians/second.

A namespace this robot does not drive is omitted, as is any individual key. Omission means UNKNOWN, never zero.

joints.description: Per-joint rate at FULL deflection, keyed exactly as descriptor.joints ("<side>_arm_<joint>.pos"), in norm_mode units per second.

task.description: Task-space jog verbs at full deflection. Present only on a robot advertising the `task_jog` capability. Note these keys are VERBS, not joints -- "yaw" is the canonical name for the task-space rotation about base Z on twist-class robots, and "shoulder_pan" is its DEPRECATED ALIAS (identical semantics; kept for existing clients -- "shoulder_pan" is not a joint name on every model). A robot advertising one advertises both while the alias lives. `z` is vertical linear motion (REP-103: + = up), an A3-class verb the L2 keymap never had -- omitted by robots that do not drive it, like any other key here. "roll" (angular about base X) is RESERVED and not yet advertised: twist ang_x stays 0.0.

yaw.description: rad/s -- canonical name for the task-space rotation about base Z

shoulder_pan.description: rad/s -- DEPRECATED alias of "yaw" (identical semantics); prefer "yaw"

base.description: Base drive at full deflection. Keyed in the JOG namespace (linear/angular), not the telemetry namespace (x.vel/theta.vel) -- see descriptor.base.

lift.description: Lift travel at full deflection, mm/s. One value: a robot with paired lifts drives both at the same rate, and A3 has a single central lift.

ranges_si.description:
The same [min, max] bounds as `ranges`, in SI units: RADIANS for a revolute joint, METRES for a prismatic one. Optional; absent means the robot does not publish it and a client MUST NOT substitute a guess. The L-series fleet is frozen and will never send it.

WHY THIS EXISTS. `ranges` is in norm_mode units, and the normalized-to-physical mapping is the robot's own PER-UNIT CALIBRATION -- not a nominal figure from the URDF. Without these bounds a client that wants real angles (to pose a URDF, run its own FK, or feed a simulator) has to substitute the URDF's nominal joint limits, which are wrong by whatever that unit's calibration offset happens to be, and wrong SILENTLY. Publishing the calibrated bounds is what makes the conversion exact.

CONVERTING. Map linearly between the two entries for the SAME key -- do NOT special-case the gripper. `ranges` already encodes the convention difference (a body joint is [-100, 100], a gripper is [0, 100]), so:
    frac = (value - ranges[k][0]) / (ranges[k][1] - ranges[k][0])
    si   = ranges_si[k][0] + frac * (ranges_si[k][1] - ranges_si[k][0])
This is the same arithmetic the daemon runs in the other direction, so a round trip is lossless up to float precision.

WHICH KEYS APPEAR. Only keys whose `ranges` entry is NORMALIZED. A key already published in physical units needs no entry and MUST NOT have one -- the A-series lift is the case in point: `ranges["lift.pos"]` is already millimetres, so converting it would be converting twice. A key present in `ranges_si` but not in `ranges` is invalid: there is nothing to map it from.

Bounds may be inverted (lower > upper) where the calibration reverses the axis. Do not sort them -- the order carries the direction, and normalizing it away flips the joint.
